38/G.goal: Explain the system-design approach for extended reality systems by framing interface and interaction design, using generic usability guidelines, and classifying XR interaction categories.
38/G.achieves: Prepares the learner to define a usable interface and interaction model for the course case study before system implementation and optimization.

38/O1.goal: Explain why XR system design focuses on interface and interaction design rather than code design and describe the basic design languages used to begin and represent design ideas.
38/O1.achieves: Gives the learner the design-stage frame needed to follow the case-study system design and later evaluate its interface and interaction choices.

38/O2.goal: Evaluate interface and interaction design choices in extended reality systems using Ben Shneiderman's Eight Golden Rules as generic design guidelines.
38/O2.achieves: Supports the course's system-development aim by letting the learner justify usable design decisions and identify usability risks before implementing the XR case study.

38/O3.goal: Identify the broad categories of extended reality interaction as object interaction, navigation, and interaction for system control.
38/O3.achieves: Gives the learner a classification for describing and later implementing navigation, object manipulation, and system-control interactions in the course case study.
